director.chapterArc: Burial ritual shifts from clinical labor to shared grief; Rook's identity reveal is a quiet, heavy confession rather than an emotional outburst.
director.restraintNote: The narrator must maintain Toren's observational distance. The weight of the scene comes from what is *not* said during the bread sharing and name revelation. Do not dramatize the grief; let the physical actions (cutting bread, opening a coat) carry the emotion.

cues.delivery: Wyck's voice is flat and physical; he speaks of his injury as a fact. The narrator observes the memory returning to Toren without internalizing it.
cues.through: He said it the way he had said it in the road cut on the second of the month, standing in more or less the same posture, with his left wrist strapped to a piece of barrel stave and three fingers he could not feel, and Toren heard the whole of that afternoon come back up the road at him and had to walk twenty paces and stand with his hands on his knees.

cues.delivery: Toren's voice cracks slightly on 'He came back' but the narrator keeps it observational. Rook is clinical and direct about searching the coat.
cues.from: Toren knew him before he got to him, from the boots, and stopped, and Rook — who was sitting on a stone twelve feet away because that was as far as he could go in one movement — said, "Yes. I saw him this morning."
cues.through: Rook looked at it for a long moment. Then he opened his coat, one-handed, slowly, because of his back, and put it in with the other four.
cues.reason: Dialogue sequence regarding the dead boy.

cues.delivery: Dessa's voice is steady and deliberate. The bread sharing must feel ritualistic but not melodramatic; the silence after 'Milo' is heavy.
cues.from: Dessa cut it. She did it poorly, in slabs, on the tailgate, with a lot of concentration, and then she stood there with the knife in her hand and the cloth in front of her and did not move for a while.
cues.through: Nobody said anything for a long time. Then Wyck said, "Right," which was not agreement with anything, and was the only thing anybody said about it, and it was enough.

cues.delivery: Rook's speech about the flask is matter-of-fact. Wyck and Senna are firm but not shouting; it is a negotiation of survival.
cues.reason: The debate over the road-ash medicine.

cues.delivery: Toren's collapse is physical and isolating. The narrator describes the sensation without over-explaining the emotion.
cues.from: Toren was sick at about the ninth hour, behind the engine house, without any warning at all.
cues.through: Wyck came down on his own at about the first hour and sat down next to Toren at the wheel without being invited, which he had never once done in a month, and put the bar across his knees.

cues.delivery: Wyck speaks with a roughness that is not anger but exhaustion. The revelation of the name must be understated.
cues.through: He said it in the morning at the stones, with all of them there.
cues.reason: Dialogue between Wyck and Toren about Rook's secret.

cues.delivery: Rook's confession is delivered with extreme restraint. The name 'Elias Marsh' lands quietly. The final lines are spoken into a silence.
cues.from: "Milo Faust," he said. "I've two things and they're both short.
cues.through: They went on north with the water going away behind them, three on their feet and two in the cart, with a hundred and twenty miles of bad road in front of them and not one wall on any of it until the end, and the whole of it to be walked, and none of it to be walked by the boy who had carried the light.
cues.reason: The identity reveal and closing narration.

pauses.after: You cannot dig a grave in a road, and you cannot dig one in an embankment either, because eleven feet down an embankment is water and everybody on that bank knew it without anybody having to say so.
pauses.reason: Scene reset after establishing the physical impossibility of digging a grave.

pauses.after: It took them most of the day. Nobody talked much. The reed fire had burned itself out along the south beds in the night and left a long black scar on the water that would be there for a year, and the smell of it was in everything, and twice Toren caught himself looking round for Milo to say something about the smell, because Milo would have said something about the smell, and that was the shape the whole day had: a series of small ordinary moments arriving one after another with nobody in them.
pauses.reason: Completed thought on the shape of the day; pause to let the absence of Milo land.

pauses.after: They laid them along the foot of the bank on the dry side and put what was left of the reed thatch out of the engine house over them, and it was not a great deal and it was what there was.
pauses.reason: Pause after covering the bodies; transition from action to the specific discovery of the boy.

pauses.after: Rook looked at it for a long moment. Then he opened his coat, one-handed, slowly, because of his back, and put it in with the other four.
pauses.reason: Breath before moving into the bread ritual.
Emphasis on the source of Dessa's knowledge and her resolve to do it right.

pauses.before: She picked up the end crust.
pauses.reason: Preparation for the start of the ritual action.

pauses.after: Toren took it and found that his hands did not want it.
pauses.reason: Pause after Toren's hands refuse to take the bread; emotional landing on his grief.
Isolating Toren's physical inability to accept the bread; a moment of grief.

pauses.after: Nobody said anything for a long time. Then Wyck said, "Right," which was not agreement with anything, and was the only thing anybody said about it, and it was enough.
pauses.reason: Major pause for silence following Milo's name in the ritual. Let the weight of the moment settle before moving to the flask scene.
Critical distinction in ownership and meaning of the flask.

pauses.after: "You're having it," said Dessa, "and I'll tell you the reason and then I'd like not to discuss it. He went out on a wall in the dark to get you across an arch. That's what it was for. That was the entire transaction and he's paid for it and if you sit here for four days being noble about a flask you will make it into nothing and I will not be able to stand it."
pauses.reason: Pause after Dessa's ultimatum; let Senna process the demand for a breath group.
Emphasis on Wyck's demand; shifting the balance of power in the negotiation.
Breath before Rook takes the medicine. A moment of shared resolve.
Confirming Rook's willingness to sacrifice himself for Senna.

pauses.after: He had been perfectly all right. He had carried stone for six hours and laid out seven men and eaten bread he did not want and had a conversation with his grandmother about the wheel, and then he walked round the corner of a brick wall to get out of the wind and put his hand flat on the brickwork and was sick until there was nothing left, and then knelt in the grass shaking with his forehead against the wall.
pauses.reason: Pause after Toren's physical collapse; transition from action to internal state.

pauses.after: Wyck came down on his own at about the first hour and sat down next to Toren at the wheel without being invited, which he had never once done in a month, and put the bar across his knees.
pauses.reason: Scene reset as Wyck approaches the wheel. Transition from Rook/Taren interaction to private conversation.
Toren's tentative question about the name; highlighting his uncertainty.

pauses.after: He said it in the morning at the stones, with all of them there.
pauses.reason: Pause before Rook steps forward; build anticipation for the confession.
Emphasis on Rook's past cruelty and the weight of this apology.

pauses.after: "My name is Elias Marsh," he said.
pauses.reason: Major pause after 'Elias Marsh' is spoken. Let the name hang in the air before Rook elaborates.
The central revelation; isolating the true identity for maximum impact.

pauses.after: Nobody said anything for a moment.
pauses.reason: Pause for Senna's response; a moment of shared recognition and relief.
